tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

qnn-setup-univariate-ideal-reuploading: Section 2.1.1 and footnote 1, pp.1-2: the authors state the univariate focus, the ideal circuit model and the data re-uploading architecture.
qnn-definition-fourier-residual: Section 2.1.1, Eqs. 3 to 5, p.2: the paper defines the partial Fourier series form and the frequency-domain residual.
qnn-target-functions-fl-fm-fh: Section 2.1.2, Eq. 8, p.3: the paper defines the three target functions.
qnn-residual-dynamics-lazy-regime: Section 2.2.1, p.3: the authors state the lazy-regime, small learning rate and constant QNTK conditions of their own derivation.
qnn-simulation-setup-noise-free: Section 3, p.4: the authors state the noise-free simulation, the CPU and GPU, and the PennyLane-based simulator.
qnn-iris-setup-and-scope: Section 3.2, p.6-7: the authors state the 2-qubit, 6-layer ansatz, the MSE loss and the purpose of the Iris task.
qnn-dlp-setup: Section 3.3, p.7: the authors state the 8-qubit, 24-layer ansatz, 40 samples, the kernel definition and the kernel-target alignment optimization.
qnn-hardware-deferred-future-work: Section 1, Remarks and Limitations, p.2: the authors leave hardware-specific experiments and theory to future work.
qnn-spectral-limits: Section 1, Remarks and Limitations, p.2: the authors state that validation uses classical simulation of ideal evolution and that the mechanism is derived for gradient-based optimization.
theorem1-retrain-components: Theorem 1, Section III, p.6: the paper defines the four time components named in the quotes.
weights-update-cost: Proof of Theorem 1, p.6: the O(Nnew d |M|) and O(Nnew d) costs are proved as Theorems 2 and 3 (Appendix B 1, Theorem 6).
theorem2-pearson-update: Theorem 2, Section IV A: stated with its conditions and proved there with explicit update formulas.
theorem3-eta-update: Theorem 3, Section IV A: stated with its conditions and proved as Theorem 6 in Appendix B 1. Table I summarizes time and memory from the stored quantities.
memory-grows-limitation: Section III, p.7: the authors state their algorithm can become memory-intensive and that stored data grows.
retrain-batch-assumption: Definition 1, Section III, p.4: the paper defines retraining with incremental batches and assumes Nnew,t much smaller than N.
build-bottlenecks-poly-n: Section II, pp.3-4: the authors state which two build components scale polynomially in N; the costs follow from their own steps.
weighted-distance-definition: Section II, Step 3, p.4: the paper defines the weighted distance and the weighted centroid.
eta-coefficient-definition: Section IV A 2, Eq. 10: the paper defines the eta coefficient as SSc over SST.
leaf-label-definitions: Section IV C, Eqs. 13 to 15, p.10: the paper defines the regression and classification leaf labels.
inference-classical-cost: Section III, p.7: the authors state that inference runs on the classical computer with cost O(kDd).
numerics-scope-classical-simulation: Section V, pp.10-11: the authors state that they evaluate only the classical QC-Forest-c because quantum-accessible data structures are unavailable.
baseline-no-feature-bagging: Section V, p.11: the authors state the sampling and baseline setup.
experiment-protocol: Section V p.11 and Appendix D 1 p.21: the authors state the ensemble size, folds, split ratio and metrics.
table3-node-counts: Appendix D 2, p.22: the authors state how the random forest node counts were matched and that no pruning is used.
qcforest-initial-build-linear: Section I.A, p.2: the authors state that initial construction takes time linear in N because the data structure is built classically.
qml-advantage-quantumly-advantageous-fun: Definition 9, Appendix B 1, p.13: the paper defines quantumly advantageous functions as HeurFBQP minus HeurFBPP/poly.
qml-advantage-concept-class-definition: Definition 10, Appendix B 1, p.13: the paper defines the concept class CN.
qml-advantage-theorem-12-quantum-learnab: Theorem 12, Appendix B 2: stated with its conditions (any D=O(poly N), any distribution, any advantageous function) and proved with Algorithm 1.
qml-advantage-lemma-11-linear-combinatio: Lemma 11, Appendix B 2: the bound 1 - D/(M+1) is stated and proved there; the quotes carry the conditions.
qml-advantage-theorem-13-quantum-evaluat: Theorem 13, Appendix B 2: stated with conditions and proved with Algorithm 2.
qml-advantage-theorem-14-classical-hardn: Theorem 14, Appendix B 3: stated with conditions and proved by contradiction through the Algorithm 3 reduction. Hardness is conditional on f being outside HeurFBPP/poly, as the definition carries.
qml-advantage-hardness-proof-technique: Appendix B 3 and Methods: the reduction proof of Theorem 14 uses the finite-field feature space as described.
qml-advantage-learning-algorithm-gaussia: Algorithm 1 and the proof of Theorem 12, Appendix B 2: Gaussian elimination and correctness of any solution are analysed there.
qml-advantage-theorem-15-quantum-data-pr: Theorem 15, Appendix C 2: stated with its conditions and proved there.
qml-advantage-two-party-setup: Protocol section, p.5 and Appendix C 1: the paper states its two-party setup.
qml-advantage-arbitrary-distribution: Methods, p.7: the authors state their result allows an arbitrary target distribution. The prior-work comparison is the authors' own description.
qml-advantage-cc-qq-separation: Appendix A 1, p.10: the authors state the CC/QQ separation they study and construct.
qml-advantage-heuristic-evaluatability-i: Appendix B 3, p.19: follows from Theorem 14 and the stated inclusion of worst-case classes in heuristic classes (Appendix A 2).
qml-advantage-existence-open-problem: New directions, item 3, p.4-5: the authors state that unconditional existence of such functions is a variant of long-standing open problems.
qml-advantage-experimental-challenge-rem: Discussion and outlook, p.7: the authors state an experimental challenge remains. The paper is purely theoretical, so the no-demonstration clause holds.
qml-advantage-function-assumption: Introduction p.2 and the Definition 9 discussion p.3: the authors state the function class and the advice-string requirement; the new value is the fuller statement.
qml-advantage-general-functions: kept HIGH at the team lead's decision: the main theorem, proved in Appendix B; team lead, 2026-10-31, Sprint 14 Manual Validation Q1 option 1 (all 28 as recommended)
qrdr-pca-definitions: Section II A, p.2: the paper defines A, Z and V_R.
qrdr-scope-basic-pca-only: Section II A, p.2: the authors state they cover basic PCA only.
qrdr-qubit-registers-setup: Section II B, p.2: the paper defines the register layout of its algorithm.
qrdr-hamiltonian-structure: Section II B, Eqs. 5 and 6, pp.2-3: the paper defines the Hamiltonian and H_lambda.
qrdr-input-requirements: Algorithm 1 and Section II B, p.3: the paper lists the inputs and the QRAM requirement for state preparation.
qrdr-algorithm-steps: Algorithm 1, p.3: the paper defines its five steps.
qrdr-off-resonance-assumption: Section II B, p.3: the authors state the assumption that c is much smaller than the minimum eigenvalue gap.
qrdr-sonar-setup: Section III A, p.6: the authors state the dataset size, R and the range of c.
qrdr-classical-simulation-scope: Figure 2 and Figure 3 captions, p.6: the authors state the quantum parts are simulated on a classical computer.
qrdr-qsvm-crossvalidation-setup: Section III A, p.6: the authors state the 8-fold split.
qrdr-qcnn-architecture: Section III B p.7 and Figures 5 and 6 p.8: the authors state the model layers, ansatz size and gate count.
qrdr-qcnn-training-setup: Section III B, pp.7-8: the authors state the networks, split, batch size, epochs, optimizer and loss.
qrdr-nisq-demonstration-limit: Section IV, p.9: the authors state that large-scale NISQ demonstrations remain challenging.
qrdr-data-availability: Section VI p.9 and reference [40]: the authors state where their supporting data are available.
qrdr-simulation-only-limit: Section I, p.2: the authors state they simulate numerically and evaluate with QSVM and QCNN; Section III repeats it. The new value is the fuller statement.
setup-data-reuploading-pqc: Section 2 and Appendix A.2: the paper defines its data re-uploading PQC and the Pauli X basis encoding.
global-approach-limit: Section 3.2, p.6: the authors state that the Bernstein approach needs large n and a very deep PQC.
pqc-scope-expressivity: Abstract, p.1: the authors state the paper investigates PQC expressivity and adds numerical experiments.

theory_low.qnn-gradient-proportional-to-residual-am: An argument from the Eq. 7 expression with no theorem or proof; the condition k within the accessible spectrum is carried by the quote, but the claim is the authors' interpretation.
theory_low.qnn-residual-exponential-solution: Eqs. 9 and 10, p.3: a direct solution of a linear difference equation under the lazy-regime, time-invariant kernel approximation; no theorem with conditions, and footnote 2 notes empirical discrepancies.
theory_low.qnn-spectral-amplitude-priority: The new value adds the lazy-regime condition stated in Section 2.2.1, p.3. The Abstract says 'prove' but the derivation is a linearization with no theorem; an authors' claim, not a proved result.
theory_low.weights-fixed-memory: Section III, p.7: the authors state fixed weight memory in prose; Table I lists it but no theorem states or proves the memory bound, so it is an authors' claim.
theory_low.theorem5-leaf-label-time: Theorem 5 is proved in Appendix C (Theorem 8) but the text layer garbles the time expression, and the main text uses epsilon4 where Appendix C uses epsilon3, so the exact statement and conditions are not settled by the quotes.
theory_low.leaf-label-estimation-method: A construction described in the Appendix C proof; it rests on amplitude estimation [54] cited from elsewhere, and no result of its own is stated in the quotes.
theory_low.qcforest-retrain-runtime: The new value matches Theorem 1 and its proof, but the proof defers clustering to cited Des-q [42], leaf labels to Appendix C, and carries eta and epsilon constants outside the poly-log; not fully proved in this paper.
theory_low.qml-advantage-theorem-18-classical-data-: Theorem 18, Appendix C 3, depends on an assumed oracle that loads the y samples in unit time and on a classically one-way permutation; the value and quotes drop the oracle condition.
theory_low.qrdr-qpe-ancilla-reduction: Section I p.2 and Section II C p.5: a resource count argued in prose, with no theorem and no count of the full circuit registers; an authors' claim.
theory_low.qrdr-resonant-transition-derivation: Section II C, Eqs. 13 to 16: a short derivation, not a labeled theorem; it holds only under the off-resonance assumption and the equations are partly lost in the text layer.
theory_low.qrdr-off-resonance-error-bound: Section II C, Eqs. 18 to 21: an inequality chain under the off-resonance assumption, not a labeled theorem, with garbled equations in the text layer.
theory_low.qrdr-evolution-query-complexity: Section II C, Eq. 22: a derived expression using cited Hamiltonian simulation costs, with no theorem or full proof in the paper.
theory_low.qrdr-total-time-complexity-eq23: Section II C, Eq. 23: a sum of three costs, two taken from cited or assumed results; no theorem.
theory_low.qrdr-table1-complexity-comparison: Table I, p.6: two of three rows come from cited prior work, and the QRDR row rests on stated assumptions; an authors' comparison.
theory_low.qrdr-qcnn-convolution-gate-count: Section III B, p.7: an O(r^3) gate-count statement whose construction is in Fig. 6(b), with no proof in the text; an authors' claim.
theory_low.qrdr-complexity: The new value adds the conditions (R, Delta_min, ||A||max) the paper requires; the bound is a derivation in prose and equations with no theorem, an authors' claim.
theory_low.thm1-multivariate-polynomial-pqc: Theorem 1, Appendix B.1: the printed proof builds (1/T) times the sum of monomial circuits, so the Hadamard test gives p(x)/T, not p(x). It also applies Lemma S5, which needs |c_alpha x^alpha| <= 1 for each monomial, though the theorem assumes only |p| <= 1. The stated exact output and counts are not established as printed.
theory_low.lemma-s5-monomial-pqc: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Lemma S5, App. B.1, p.20: the proof opens 'By Corollary S2, there exist d single-qubit PQCs ...'. Corollary S2 (App. A.2, p.18) is the quantum signal processing existence result taken from [47], cited and not proved here. The product construction and the counts are proved, but the existence of each factor rests on the cited result. The same group graded Lemma S14 LOW for its cited Lemma S11 [54].
theory_low.prop-s7-trigonometric-pqc: Proposition S7: the proof is stated as similar to Theorem 1 and is not written out, and Theorem 1's proof has a normalization gap.
theory_low.lemma-s9-bernstein-pqc: Lemma S9, Appendix C.2: the proof's own counts (depth O(d (n+1)^(d+1) log(n+1)), parameters (n+1)^d (n+2)^d) are larger than the stated O(d n^d log n) and O(d n^d), and it relies on Theorem 1's construction.
theory_low.lemma-s9-proof-counts: Appendix C.2, p.25: intermediate counts in a proof that disagree with the lemma statement; the 'after simplification' step is not shown.
theory_low.thm2-universal-approximation: Theorem 2: existence of n follows from Bernstein convergence, but its stated size counts rest on Lemma S9, whose proof counts disagree with its statement, and on Theorem 1's proof.
theory_low.thm3-lipschitz-bound: Theorem 3: the error bound is printed garbled with constants differing from Lemma S8, and the circuit size rests on Lemma S9.
theory_low.lemma-s14-localization-pqc: Lemmas S12 and S14: the statements are garbled in the text layer, so the conditions are not settled by the quotes, and the proof uses a cited sign-function approximation (Lemma S11 [54]).
theory_low.lemma-s15-taylor-coefficient-pqc: Lemma S15: statement garbled in the text layer; a point-fitting construction whose angles are fixed from the target's derivatives.
theory_low.lemma-s17-taylor-pqc: Lemma S17, Appendix D.3: the proof is the single line 'The Theorem 1', so it rests on Theorem 1's construction, which has a normalization gap.
theory_low.thm4-holder-bound: Theorem 4, Appendix D.3: the proof goes from Eq. D.64/D.65 to D.66 by dropping the first term (the Taylor-polynomial mismatch) with no argument, and the nested circuit is built from a rounded expectation value. Sizes rest on Theorem 1 and Lemma S17.
theory_low.cor-s18-l2-bound: Corollary S18, Appendix D.3: rests on Theorem 4, whose proof drops a term. The 4dK^(1-d) bound is not derived from the text, which says only that nu is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure; a quantitative bound needs more (for example a bounded density).
theory_low.d4-global-vs-local-lipschitz: Appendix D.4: derived by the authors from Theorems 3 and 4; the s=0 case is outside Theorem 4's stated hypothesis.
theory_low.e-size-measure-and-scalings: Appendix E: a substitution into upper bounds of two constructions; an authors' comparison, with no lower bound.
theory_low.e-parameter-count-scalings: Appendix E: a comparison of authors' upper bounds with a cited ReLU bound; no lower bound on either side.
theory_low.pqc-approx-bounds: The new value is more exact than the stored one (Lipschitz and Holder cases, trifling region, no rate in Theorem 2). It is the paper's own claim to establish bounds, but its proofs have gaps (Theorem 1 normalization, Lemma S9 counts, Theorem 4 dropped term), so not a proved result.
theory_low.pqc-vs-relu-size: The new value adds the stated simplifications (constant error, terms in s as constants, d much larger than s); it compares the authors' upper bounds with a cited upper bound, an authors' claim.
